extraction.methodology_summary: The authors construct forward-looking currency implied volatilities using OTC option prices via a model-free approach. They estimate a dynamic volatility network through time-varying parameter vector autoregression (TVP-VAR) models, isolating shocks that exclude contemporaneous common correlations. Currencies are sorted monthly into quintiles based on to-directional and from-directional volatility connectedness, forming long-short zero-cost portfolios to test currency return predictability.
extraction.universe: 20 developed and emerging market countries against the USD

performance_metrics.context: Short-term to-directional volatility connectedness long-short strategy (T(S))
Long-term to-directional volatility connectedness long-short strategy (T(L))

key_findings: Currencies that transmit more correlation-adjusted volatility shocks earn lower average excess returns.
Buying the weakest and selling the strongest transmitters of correlation-adjusted volatility shocks yields strong risk-adjusted returns driven primarily by spot exchange rate movements.
A general equilibrium model confirms that volatility transmission captures idiosyncratic country-specific jump risks, matching empirical findings.
The volatility transmission strategy provides substantial diversification benefits when combined with standard currency benchmarks due to weak negative correlations.
